description: Interested in the fascinating stories of lost NASA equipment and passionate about storytelling in an interesting, interactive and playful way.
summary:
Apollo 13: A Successful Failure is an educational computer and board game, that retells the Apollo 13 mission.
The story is divided in 12 chapters, in which critical for the story events happen. The route on the rocket in the main menu is the free-return trajectory that Apollo 13 followed.
Each chapter has story cards with a small text and colourful word units, in order to be adapted to children and adults with ADHD. There are also relevant quizzes and games, such as aiming with the COAS telescope, and rolling dice to achieve the number of the re-entry angle. There is also a Saturn V demonstration which explains each basic part of the rocket.
The game runs in Greek and English and has music with a volume control.
For classroom or print use, there is a PDF board with a QR code at each station, plus instructions for building a paper-roll spaceship from kitchen roll, cardboard and paint.
details: This interactive story offers knowledge about the Apollo13 mission in an interesting and fun way. It is designed for children from 8 years old and adults with ADHD. A recording to be heard along with the appearing words was recorded, but didn't work and will be created just after the competition's end. I used Claude to build an html code to help me create my vision the game.
